evals.prompt: What effects can I put on my photo?
evals.expected_output: The five-group menu of 45 effects with labels, one-line looks and the start input each needs, then a question asking which one to apply and for the photo.
assertions: The reply lists effects grouped as camera and motion, clones and identity, world and transformation, art and style, and product creature and spectacle.
Each listed effect names the start input it needs (a person photo, a product photo, a vehicle, or a source clip).
The reply asks the user to pick one effect and supply the asset; it does not start generation.
The reply states that Higgsfield-style names are menu labels and the skill is not affiliated.

evals.prompt: Apply Street colossus to this full-body photo of me standing on a sidewalk and generate it.
evals.expected_output: A run that fits the photo to the recipe, builds a giant start frame with Seedream because the raw photo has no city scale, fills the street-colossus template with counts and cut times, runs prompt-review, registers the request, submits one 480p draft with the giant frame as first_frame, inspects it, and asks before any final.
assertions: The photo is hashed and checked against the Start photo contract before any prompt is written.
A Seedream start frame of the same person at building height on a city street is generated, reviewed and approved before it is used as the first frame.
The prompt keeps the recipe's two hard cuts at 4s and 7s, one helicopter, exact pedestrian and taxi counts, and the outfit described once.
The Seedance request uses role first_frame, draft true, resolution 480p, generate_audio false and no camera_fixed or seed field.
prompt-review runs on the Seedance prompt and the Seedream prompt and resolves CRITICAL and MAJOR findings before submission.
The provider task ID is saved as soon as it is acknowledged and the same task is polled after a timeout.
After the draft the reply reports QA against the recipe's checks and asks before a 1080p promotion with a cost estimate.

evals.prompt: Do the Eyes in effect on this close-up portrait.
evals.expected_output: The eyes-in recipe with the opening framing slot set to an extreme close portrait, the push-in timeline, and an ending on pure black, as a first_frame draft.
assertions: The 0-1s beat matches the first frame (extreme close portrait), not a medium shot.
The prompt states no blink, one round pupil and a uniform black frame from 6.5s.
The eye side is named by frame side.
The route is i2v-first-frame with generate_audio false.

evals.prompt: Run Clones on my photo but I need exactly 5 copies.
evals.expected_output: The clones recipe with the count stated at every timestamp, plus a warning that the model overshot the count in the probe and an offer to request 4 or revise after the draft.
assertions: The prompt states 1 figure, then exactly 5 copies plus the original (6 figures) from 3.5s.
The reply warns that counts ran high in the probe and that the count is treated as approximate.
Each copy has one face and one outfit and its own idle pose.
The reply does not claim the exact count is guaranteed.

evals.prompt: Make the Comic effect on my 5 second clip.
evals.expected_output: A hand-off to seedance-restyle with the comic style block, the source-clip requirements, the muted master, and the post-audio route, since the effect is video-to-video.
assertions: The route is v2v-restyle and the restyle contract (muted master, generate_audio false, no baked text) applies.
The reply asks for the source clip and a rights statement for the footage and the people in it.
No image-to-video prompt is written for a photo.
Real people in the clip route through Virtual Portrait identity anchors, not a liveness check.

evals.prompt: Do Particles on my portrait and put readable labels like 'SUBJECT 01' on the screen.
evals.expected_output: A text-free generated clip plus a post step: the labels are authored with html-graphic-render or HyperFrames and composited, not prompted into the video.
assertions: The Seedance prompt contains no label text, HUD words or numbers.
The reply routes the labels to HyperFrames or html-graphic-render in post.
The route is composite and generate_audio is false.
The reply says Particles has a thin description and that its recipe is an untested hypothesis.

evals.prompt: Just write me the Smash and grab prompt for my lip balm tube, don't generate anything.
evals.expected_output: A prompt-only package: the recipe's template filled for an unlabelled or labelled tube, no files and no submission, with the label coming from a real asset and not from generation.
assertions: The run stops after prompt composition and review; it creates no project files and submits nothing.
The product is described positively with no invented lettering; the label clause matches whether the tube is labelled.
The brand label, if any, is stated to come from the user's real photo or an authorized asset, never generated.
The thief outfit is written once and repeated verbatim in both shots; the hard cut is at 7.6s.
